title: Package descriptions across ecosystems — and the three catalog rules that cannot fire

census.why: PHP's manifest, read by the JSON extractor and decided by a rule.
TOML, read as JSON Pointers so `cargo.package.description` fires with no change to the rule. The rule was never wrong; nothing had ever given it a document to match against.
The same reader, the same pointers, a second rule revived. One extractor, two rules — which is the argument for writing the reader rather than weakening the rules.

No longer read as prose. A Dockerfile is instructions, and treating `RUN apt-get install -y build-essential` as a paragraph the classifier had to talk itself out of was a precision bug in its own right. Emitting `/LABEL/org.opencontainers.image.description` also gives `docker.label` the key it always matched on.

expectations.find: Le noyau de l'atelier, en PHP
expectations.why: Rendered on Packagist. Cited to a rule, so the verdict is traceable.
Rendered on pub.dev, and the field pub.dev scores a package on.

expectations.find: Le noyau de l'atelier, en Rust
expectations.why: Registry-visible copy, cited to the rule that was written for it and had never once fired.
The same field in the same format for a different ecosystem, and the second half of what one TOML reader bought.

expectations.find: Un atelier de publication pour petites équipes
expectations.why: An OCI image label. The rule matches on a KEY, and the prose extractor's key was `p[0]` — so the defect was never in the rule, and rewriting the rule to match `p[0]` would have claimed every line of every Dockerfile as translatable prose.
A version constraint one line from a field that must be translated.
